critic:wiring-and-code.verdict:
NOT READY in the wiring lens. The verdict is the same for A without the lock (the pick), A with the lock (the same canopy turned 105 deg), today and B, because my probe gives the same gaps in all four. The canopy still cannot be wired as drawn. The cord ends 1.0 mm under the driver. The named Heyco bushings are 11 to 11.5 mm long and sit in gaps of 2.0 to 10 mm. ERP wants the driver screwed flat by its two tabs, which covers one of the two centre entries whichever face it goes on. This is blocking, but it can be fixed inside the 50 mm canopy without the owner, unless a taller canopy is chosen.
The grounding and code are close behind it. The enclosure's bond is sound, everything below the canopy is Class 2, and the splice room passes even by UL 1598 6.16 (7.0 in3 needed, 8.5 free), though the text cites NEC 314.16. Still to fix: 'tap after anodising' on the canopy's drawing; one ground-screw build (PEM nut or extrusion), with a cupped washer and a real screw length; the enclosure and cover callouts and tabs; UL 1598 6.17.2 separation for the Class 2 cord connection made at installation and for 0-10 V; the stale texts.

findings.claim:
The canopy still cannot be wired as drawn, in all four tops (A with the lock has the same canopy turned 105 deg). Both wire entries are on the axis: the supply comes down through a snap bushing in the enclosure's top, and the Class 2 cord comes up through a strain-relief bushing in its cover. The 84 x 40 driver covers the axis wherever it sits in the 62 x 98 interior, and turned 90 deg it does not fit. Three problems follow.
- The drawn cord ends 1.0 mm under the driver, so it cannot reach the driver's output leads.
- The parts the BOM names do not fit the gaps: a Heyco 7/8 in snap bushing above the driver, and a Heyco strain-relief bushing in the cover.
- ERP says the driver must be screwed down flat through its two tabs. On either flat face (the top or the cover) it would sit over one of the two entries. The CAD floats it 2.0 mm above the cover with no fixing, and the BOM and drawings name none.
This is the v8 blocking item ('the parts it names do not fit') in a new form. One way that fits the 50 mm canopy:
- screw the driver by its tabs under the enclosure's top;
- take its input leads out at its input end and splice in the outlet box (UL 1598 6.15.1.6);
- bring the cord up through a low grommet into the 11.8 mm left under the driver. No strain relief is required on a cable-hung lamp's cord (11.6.6).

The cord is cut to length and wired to the driver at installation. That is a Class 2 connection made at installation, in the same compartment as the 120 V splices also made there. Nothing keeps the two apart: no barrier, no defined route, no 6.4 mm spacing. NOTES also offer 0-10 V dimming, whose control wires could only arrive through the supply's own opening and bushing. Separately, the strain-relief bushing has to be squeezed onto the cord at installation with Heyco's pliers, a tool the lamp does not ship with.

The splice-room figure passes, but on the wrong rule. A luminaire's own field-wiring compartment falls under UL 1598 6.16, not NEC 314.16. UL 1598 does not 'send the count to the NEC'.
- 6.16 counts 12 AWG branch conductors, plus the driver's leads and the cord's conductors.
- That needs 114.8 cm3 (7.0 in3) here, against 139.7 cm3 (8.5 in3) free by my probe and 7.9 in3 by the lane, so the enclosure passes.
- The enclosure's drawing prints the NEC figure instead.
The wired-sample route (6.16.4: every conductor 150 mm inside, the cover fitted without damage) cannot be done until the blocking finding is fixed. The free room is in thin slots (11.0 mm side channels, 10.0 over the driver, 7.0 at the ends), so the instructions should name lever-type connectors: twist-on connectors are wider than the slots.

The grounding screw's terminal is ordered two ways.
- The plate's drawing orders a PEM CLS-032 clinch nut.
- The CAD, BOM and NOTES order a downward-extruded tapped hole with 'five threads'.
The drawn extrusion (Ø8 x 2.4 below the 1.6 sheet) needs about four times the steel a Ø4 hole gives, so 'five threads' is optimistic (UNVERIFIED; it depends on the tooling).
Still not fixed from v8: the cupped washer or two raised areas (UL 1598 6.14.2.9(d)).
The '10-32 x 3/16' green screw is not a stock length I could find. The stock green 10-32 screw (3/8 in), in the drawn thread, stands 3.5 to 5.5 mm above the plate's top onto the ceiling.
The tip as drawn (0.8 above, no wire under the head) is harmless: with the EGC under the head it sits 0.9 to 1.3 below the top face.

The canopy's set-screw bond is an acceptable means and needs no jumper, if it passes the bonding test. The screw threads are cut through the anodise into bare metal, and the cup bites the bare zinc of the plate's rim. But 'tap after anodising' appears only in the BOM row, not on the canopy's drawing. A shop's normal order is to tap and then anodise, which insulates the threads, so the drawing must say it. The same sheet still prints the v6 note ('gland ... its nut flush', 'two Ø6 holes at r 40', 'held to the strap'), which contradicts its own callout.

The new sheet-steel drawings give outline sizes only. The enclosure and the cover carry no hole, thread or tab callouts, and the CAD's holes are not makeable or are the wrong kind.
- The cover's M3 holes sit in 8 x 4 tabs, 0.5 mm from the tab's free edge and 0.5 mm from the inside of its bend, in 1.0 mm sheet. A shop cannot tap that.
- The M4 and M3 holes are drawn at the screws' own diameter, with no clearance.
- The cover's Ø14 round hole suits no Heyco strain relief: those need a 12.7 D-hole.
- The top's Ø22.0 is 0.2 under the 7/8 in bushing's hole.
- Nothing says how the corners of the five-sided box are closed.
- No deburr note (UL 1598 5.1.3).
Electrical rows and notes still describe v8 or earlier, or name no type.

The supply path is otherwise sound, with three points left to the lab or the instructions.
- The plate's 'rolled' Ø22 is right for 1.6 sheet. It is 3.8 cm2 directly under the box, against 11.4.4's 2.6 cm2, and relies on the enclosure's top 4 mm below acting as a baffle. That is the lab's call.
- The EGC must leave the plate's opening and run about 45 mm in the 4.0 mm plate-to-enclosure gap to the green screw just past the enclosure's end. It must dodge the box screw's head (1.6 mm over the enclosure) and pass over the snap bushing's head. A bare 12 AWG fits; an insulated one is tight. NOTES never say where or when the EGC lands.
- The canopy's flush grommet is a made part with no drawing and no bore-edge radius called out (5.14.1).

findings.claim:
Sound in this lens:
- The enclosure is 1.0 steel, far above the minimum.
- The enclosure is bonded by serrated M4 screws into PEM SO-M4-4 standoffs in Ø7.14 holes.
- Everything below the canopy is Class 2 below the shock limit, so it needs no grounding.
- The steel cables carry the lamp, and the cord needs no strain relief.
- The 4 in outlet box and the 1.6 plate carry about 2.75 kg, far under 50 lb.
- The box screws now go in before the enclosure.
- The Lapp gland is gone; the flush black grommet keeps the 11 Nov look.

What a UL or ETL engineer will still ask. None of it is unsafe in itself.
- The driver is Recognized, not Listed: UL 8750 Recognized Class 2. The lab applies its conditions of acceptability.
- Fix the driver by its tabs.
- Rate and mark the lamp 120 V.
- Settle 6.15.1.6 (supply leads reaching 150 mm into the outlet box) against splicing in the lamp's own compartment.
- Instructions should name 'a 4 in round or octagon outlet box designed for luminaire support (NEC 314.27(A)(2))', not 'junction box'; where the EGC lands; how the cord is cut and terminated; which connectors to use.
- Tests: bonding (18.2), ground screw (17.39), support loading of the cable fasteners (17.15 via 5.10.9), normal temperature (11.6.10 (USA): 60 C at the supply connections, or mark), and the wired sample (6.16.4).
- If the lab tests the cover's bushing as a strain relief (156 N, 17.21.1), the 1.0 cover, held only at its ends, bends until the bushing lands on the canopy grommet 0.2 mm below.

The bayonet, seat and swap now hold both in the CAD and in what the package buys: one way in, all three pins bearing level, 0 clashes, the detent clear. Six things still need fixing: the enclosure and cover sheets give no holes and their M3 tabs cannot be made; the strain relief is unnamed and drawn 3.2 tall where a real one needs more room; the set screws are bought 0.8 too long to sit flush; the cord step's 'fixed run' is defined nowhere; NOTES do not say where the canopy sits during levelling; the detent's named plunger has a Ø3 ball, not the drawn Ø2.5. findings.claim: All four packages. The cord step cannot be followed to a number. NOTES say the cord, from the lamp's grip to the strain relief, is 'the cables' length plus 2 mm plus the fixed run inside the canopy (marked on the cord)'. Nowhere is the fixed run given a length or a start and end point, and the cables' length has no start and end point either. In the CAD the strain relief grips the cord (z 730.2 to 733.4) level with the grippers' cable ends (732.5). The cables run 607.3 from the cap's top (r 16, z 126) to the grippers, and the cord runs 606.9 straight from the grip's top (124.5) to the cover (731.4). So 'cables' length + 2' alone gives the drawn 2 mm of slack and the stated 2 cm bow (23 mm by my arc). Adding the canopy's own run (floor 726 to cover 731.4, 5.4) gives about 7.8 mm of slack and a bow of about 42 mm, twice what NOTES state and the pictures show. Under that reading the cord never carries the lamp. But the step is done 'with the canopy still down', so a cable measured only as far as the lowered canopy would leave the cord short, and the cord would then carry the lamp. The cord row is also stale: it still says 'one [grip] in the canopy' and '2 mm longer than the cables between its grips'. Fix: drop the fixed run. Mark the cord, measured beside a cable from where both leave the cap, 2 mm past the gripper's lower end (609 for the 600 drop), and put the strain relief's lower face at the mark.

findings.claim: All four packages; this affects hanging level. NOTES level the lamp with 'the canopy hanging on them below the plate', but the canopy cannot hang freely there. Its Ø3 floor holes at r 48 bind on the splayed cables after a drop of only 7 mm (8 for B). To reach the grippers it must come down 50 to 150 mm, which spreads the cables with about 0.4 to 0.5 N each. That is fine while it is held. Let go, it slides on down (my estimate, mu 0.2 to 0.3) to 33 to 49 mm above the cap. There it pushes each cable out about 29 mm and lifts the lamp 9 to 14 mm. A 1 mm difference between the two pushes changes the level by 0.8 to 1.2 deg, which is the whole 1 deg target, and the reading then shifts when the canopy goes up. Held 50 to 150 mm below the plate, it shortens each cable by at most 0.25 mm. Fix: say in NOTES to hold the canopy 5 to 15 cm below the plate during levelling (tape it to the cord or the cables), or cut the floor's cable holes as short radial slots (r 44 to 50) so it hangs free.
